ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree-Law 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) Article 13 and 14 requiring identification of ultimate beneficial owners for SL registration; Law 10/2010 of April 28, 2010 on prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing (Ley 10/2010), as amended by Law 6/2023 of March 30, 2023; Royal Decree 304/2014 of May 5, 2014 establishing the AML/CFT regulatory framework; Royal Decree 6/2023 of November 30, 2023 updating beneficial ownership registration; Regulation (EU) 2015/849 (4th AMLD) and Regulation (EU) 2018/843 (5th AMLD) transposed into Spanish Law 10/2010; Spanish Companies Registry Regulation (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, Real Decreto 1784/1996), Articles 81-87 on UBO identification; Moncloa Decision of 2023 and recent amendments requiring mandatory beneficial ownership filing to the central Spanish UBO Register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) before incorporation completion; Royal Decree 163/2024 (January) reinforcing the beneficial ownership register enforcement regime for SLs.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (1) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (2) EU Council Financial Sanctions Database; (3) Spanish Ministry of Economy's List of Persons Subject to Restrictive Measures (Registro de Sanciones Financieras, administered by SEPBLAC); (4) OFAC SDN List (for international exposure); (5) UK HMT Sanctions List (where applicable); (6) Interpol Red Notices for politically exposed individuals; (7) PEP designation consistent with FATF recommendation 12 and Law 10/2010 Article 14; and (8) domestic Spanish Anti-Money Laundering Commission (SEPBLAC) records. Screening must be carried out on every director, shareholder and UBO with ownership ≥25%, prior to notary execution and repeated within 5 business days before the deed date. Enhanced due diligence applies where a shareholder/corporate group domiciled in a high-risk third country (FATF-listed) or where any PEP is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online name clearance certificate, via the Registradores de España portal — Name certificate request (Certificación de Denominación Social) through the website www.registradores.org / www.registro-mercantil-central.com.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or translated/adapted to Spanish-proper orthography. Foreign words are permitted only if they are sufficiently generic, not deceptive, and follow the Spanish phonetics/transliteration doctrine set by the Registro Mercantil Central. The exact name must be transmissible in Latin script; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin script for registration, with the Spanish version the controlling legal name. All names must be unique, not misleading, and cannot be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names in Spain; names may be in Spanish or co-official languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician) but must remain compatible with central registry processing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Spain / España / Estado / Gobierno / Administración General del Estado / Ministerio / Societat
Bank / Banco / Caixa / Caja / Financiera / Financiero / Cooperativa de Crédito (unauthorized use of 'bank' or 'credit cooperative' prohibited without Bank of Spain authorization)
Insurance / Seguros / Aseguradora / Mutua de Seguros (requires authorization by the Directorate of Insurance and Pension Funds)
Bolsa / Mercado de Valores / Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores / CNMV / Stock Market (requires securities authority consent)
Oficial / Organismo Público / Público / Administración / Ministerio / Consejo / Colegio / Instituto/Centro de Investigación (only with express prior approval of the competent public authority)
Real / Patrimonio Nacional / Casa Real / Rey / Reina / Príncipe / Infanta (royal/state symbolism requiring official authorization)
Internacional / Global / Mundial / Mundial de España / Unión Europea / UE / Euro (only if objectively justified by the business scope and not likely to deceive the market)
Fundación / Sociedad Laboral / Cooperativa / Asociación (if the intended structure is not of that legal type)

Policía / Guardia Civil / Ejército / Fuerzas Armadas / Interpol / Federación / Confederación / organismo oficial (terms evoking armed/security or federation bodies require prior institutional authorization)
IG / Impuesto / Hacienda / Ministerio de Hacienda / Tesoro / Adscripción estatal (misleading fiscal/state terms)
Particularly protected words: 'Nacional', 'Central', 'España', 'Estatal', 'Gobierno', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Diputación', 'Consejería', 'Secretaría de Estado' — all require official authorization.
Terms that infringe trademarks or notified trade names
Words contrary to public order, public morality, or discriminatory/hateful terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A positive name certificate is valid for 30 days (renewable for a further 30 days only once upon payment and prior to expiry). Where the name certificate is rejected by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration request (recurso de reposición) with the same Registro within 1 month of the rejection; alternatively, a direct administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be addressed to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within a 1-month deadline. The appeal must demonstrate absence of identity/confusion with pending registrations and may attach prior trademark clearances and statutory dilution arguments. A dossier of alternative names should be submitted simultaneously; if all are rejected, the applicant can re-file with a modified name, and, if still denied, the applicant may pursue judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered address (domicilio social) in Spain for an SL engaged in ISIC 3240 (silicone stress relief fidget manufacturing) provided the address is registered at a real physical location in Spain that can receive official notifications. Pure virtual office arrangements without dedicated physical premises or staff are accepted by the registry but create elevated commercial substance scrutiny by the Tax Agency (AEAT) when applying for VAT (modelo 036) and corporate tax obligations. Given that the business is a manufacturing (handling food-grade silicone) operation, the permissibility is conditional: the virtual office must have a physical mailbox and a service arrangement; but the enterprise must establish a real production/warehouse facility in Spain within the first fiscal year to substantiate the 'manufacturing' tax and social security profile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 50% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) in the context of VAT refund checks or municipal licensing; 35% likelihood of inspection by the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales if the company shows unexplained transactions; and 70% likelihood for manufacturing-site inspection under the IE-CNAE 3240 classification if, during the first 2 years, municipal authorities (ayuntamiento) perform an on-site licensing check of the registered production facility (industrial license / IAE). Overall aggregate quantified likelihood: 45-55% within the first 24 months given manufacturing risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital; principally Articles 4, 12-21, 22, 23, 28, 58-59, 62-64, and 78.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Madrid) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office for inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary; submitted through the CIRCE system or physically to the competent Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada mandates a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash or in kind at incorporation; for cash contributions, the capital must be deposited in a blocked account at a Spanish credit institution and the corresponding deposit certificate attached to the public deed (Art. 78 LSC). No separate governmental escrow is required; the deposit is released upon Mercantile Registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the Sole Shareholder unanimously, that: (1) The Company is duly constituted as a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under the Spanish Ley de Sociedades de Capital according to the public deed executed before the Notary; (2) the subscribed share capital of EUR 3,000 has been fully paid in cash as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate; (3) the registered office is established at Calle de la Industria 84, 28004 Madrid, Spain; (4) [FOUNDER_NAME] is appointed Sole Administrator, with full corporate powers under Articles 62 and following of the LSC, to manage and represent the Company; (5) the Sole Administrator is expressly authorized to obtain the Tax Identification Number, execute all proceedings before the Mercantile Registry, and open corporate bank accounts. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain positive name certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Calle María de Molina 50, 28006 Madrid, Spain (online via CIRCE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application for a negative certification of company name (certificación de denominación social) with two proposed corporate names in priority order. The Registry verifies no identical or confusingly similar company name exists. Upon issuance, the certificate is valid for two months and must be attached to the public deed. Submit the notarial request via the CIRCE portal or by direct application at the Registry counter.
required_dossiers: DNI or passport of founder
Two alternative proposed corporate names
Online application form or physical application letter
Proof of payment of the certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected due to similarity, immediately file a new application with additional alternative names; if the application quere has a technical defect, correct the form and resubmit through the same portal within the remaining validity window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a blocked capital deposit account and obtain deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank or savings bank) with an office in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founder opens a temporary bank account in the company's intended name, deposits at least EUR 3,000, and requests a certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) confirming full payment. The certificate must expressly state that the amount is provisionally blocked for incorporation purposes and will be disposed of only by the administrators or the notary once the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Copy of the accepted name certificate
DNI/passport and NIE of the founder
Completed draft provisional bylaws for the notary (sometimes requested by the bank)
Bank's own client due-diligence form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account without a NIF, ask the notary for a provisional NIF code or use the alternative 'civil liability insurance' capital guarantee mechanism recognized by Art. 78.2 LSC; if the certificate is incorrectly worded, request a corrected certificate before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public incorporation deed before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Colegio Notarial de Madrid or any Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft bylaws and all supporting documents to the selected notary. The notary reviews legal capacity, capital payment, and legality of the corporate object, then signs the escritura pública de constitución. The notary also applies electronically for the provisional NIF (código de identificación fiscal) and may file the deed electronically for registration.
required_dossiers: Positive name certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil Central
Bank deposit certificate for EUR 3,000
Draft bylaws aligned with Articles 22-30 LSC
Founder's passport/DNI and NIE, plus proof of tax address in Spain
Optional/required governing agreement with foreign ownership (no special approval required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in documents or bylaws, cure by amending the draft deed or filing a standalone correction deed (escritura de subsanación) before the same notary; if a founder lacks a valid NIE, the notary can request a provisional NIE code at the time of deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the deed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of Madrid (or province of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the deed electronically to the Provincial Mercantile Registry, or the legal representative submits a paper copy. The Registrar reviews the deed and bylaws against LSC requirements. Once accepted, the company acquires legal personality and the directors' liability becomes effective. The registration is published free of charge in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil).
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation
Name certificate or certification of its validity
Bank deposit certificate or capital guarantee certificate
Formalized notarial application for registration
Confirmation of payment of registry filing fees
Fiscal classification form (if requested preliminarily)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a suspension (suspensión) or defect note, the legal representative or notary must submit the missing or corrective document within the statutory term; resubmission after cure is generally completed within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain final NIF and complete tax census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Main Office Madrid or competent local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file Form 036/037 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) with AEAT to obtain the definitive tax identification number (NIF) and register the company in the income tax and VAT obligations. Provide proof of registration from the Mercantile Registry. The final NIF replaces the provisional NIF obtained before the deed.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscription in the Mercantile Registry
Provisional NIF certificate
Public deed of incorporation
Form 036 or 037 duly completed
Statistical declaration of business start-up (if requested by AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT rejects the NIF application due to a mismatch of data, correct the information in the 036 form and resubmit electronically; any query on the economic activity code should be resolved by selecting the correct IAE code for 'Manufacture of games and toys (ISIC 3240)'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company as an employer with social security and file mandatory movement of workers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and Dirección General de Trabajo (Ministry of Labour)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before hiring employees, the company must obtain an employer registration number (código de cuenta de cotización). File Form TA.6 with TGSS and simultaneously declare the industrial legalization and workplace safety formation (Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo). Appoint a prevention service and register the workplace opening communication (comunicación de apertura del centro de trabajo) with the Labour Authority.
required_dossiers: Certified NIF certificate
Mercantile Registry registration certificate
Company's IAE economic activity registration
Form TA.6 (solicitud de inscripción del empresario)
Workplace safety plan signed by the appointed prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS returns the request for missing document, supply the missing item and resubmit within five working days; if the activity classification is challenged, request reassignment based on ISIC 3240 / CNAE 3240 with the supporting municipal license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal activity license and industrial environmental clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the registered office and plant are located (e.g., Junta Municipal de Distrito, Área de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for a municipal activity license (licencia de actividad) and, if required, an environmental operating authorization (licencia ambiental or communication previa). This includes confirming the location is zoned for industrial use, submitting technical plans of the workshop, a noise and emission technical report, and a fire safety compliance plan. In Madrid, proceed through the 'Licencia Ambiental Unificada' or 'Declaración Responsable' depending on the activity's environmental classification.
required_dossiers: Municipal application form (instancia general)
Technical project signed by competent technician (localización/puesta en marcha)
NIF and Mercantile Registry certificate
Fire safety and load-bearing certificate from a qualified surveyor
Environmental impact classification request (Form IAE / municipal form)
Proof of official fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal activity file is queried, the company is granted a deadline to submit the missing architect/engineer plans or environmental technical reports; if the license is denied based on zoning, appeal to the municipal administrations civic review committee or apply for a waiver for a non-conforming existing use.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community of Madrid (or corresponding regional authority) and the municipal Ayuntamiento's Licencia de Actividad department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia ambiental unificada / Licencia de actividad económica (or communication previa) for the compression molding of food-grade silicone articles and novelty fidget toys

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Economía Circular y de Protección Ambiental, Viceconsejería de Medio Ambiente, Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Simplified environmental registration / evaluation (Evaluación Ambiental Simplificada) — Category C in the regional Sectorial and Technical Standard; the activity is not automatically exempt because silicone molding uses heat, potentially generating VOCs and noise, but qualifies as a low-scale manufacturing activity requiring an environmental registration rather than a full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: maximum volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in treated air must stay below 50 mg C/m3 in any extraction stream (EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU, solvent gate). Wastewater discharges to municipal sewer must meet DOO < 1000 mg O2/L, SST < 600 mg/L, pH 6-9; silicone waste and raw silicone compounds must be segregated as solid non-hazardous waste (L.E.R. 07 08 99) and managed by an authorized waste manager; any silica dust from trimming/polishing shall be captured with HEPA filtration to avoid exceedance of workplace dust limits of 4 mg/m3 respirable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The industrial premise must obtain a fire safety certificate from the Bomberos / local civil defense service, verifying that means of escape, fire extinguishers, and emergency lighting comply with the municipal Condiciones de Protección contra Incendios. In addition, a structural load inspection by a competent engineer is required for the molding presses and storage racks. A positive workplace safety audit (seguridad e higiene) from the joint health and safety prevention service is necessary before employee deployment; for activities with food-grade silicone contact, the company must also hold an EU Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 food contact compliance statement and a hygiene validation under any applicable Spanish national requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Spanish Tax Administration Agency; official e-office (Sede Electrónica): https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident entity with Spanish taxable nexus, the foreign company must appoint a Spanish tax representative (unless exempt under an EU Directive or applicable DTA) and file Form 036 (Censo de obligados tributarios) with AEAT to obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the entity; the same form simultaneously requests the VAT registration number (NIF-IVA). Required supporting documents include a notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation, proof of the entity's legal existence, an original power of attorney granted to the tax representative, and identification of the ultimate beneficial owner(s). Registration must be completed before the commencement of any taxable activity in Spain; if the company undertakes only occasional taxable transactions, a provisional registration may be made for that specific transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide U.S.-style 'check-the-box' elections. An SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on its worldwide income. Available optional regimes include (i) group taxation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal) for a Spanish tax group; (ii) the venture-capital vehicle regimes (SCR/SCA); and (iii) tax transparency for Uniones Temporales de Empresas (UTE), which does not apply to corporations. Hybrid mismatch treatment is governed by ATAD transposition rules and only operates to disallow deductions or require inclusions where mismatches arise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido – IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold exists in Spain; any entity making taxable supplies or services in the course of economic activity must register for Spanish VAT from the first euro of taxable turnover unless the transaction is purely sporadic or the entity is covered by a specific exemption. For non-established EU suppliers, the intra-EU distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 applies, above which registration in Spain is mandatory. SMEs may access the simplified regime (régimen simplificado) and the special agricultural regime, but such regimes do not exempt the entity from VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain has phased mandatory electronic invoicing under Royal Decree 1007/2023 and Ley Crea y Crece: from summer 2025, taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 8 million must issue electronic invoices; all other business-to-business taxpayers must do so from 2026. Invoicing must comply with the Facturae XML format or another AEAT-accepted structured format. In addition, large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6 million) and all those registered under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system must transmit invoice records to AEAT electronically within 4 days of each invoice's issuance (near-real-time fiscal reporting). SII submissions are validated against AEAT's API and may be rejected or accepted automatically; rejected records must be corrected and re-submitted within the statutory deadline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate (exemption with deductibility) applies to the export of tangible goods from Spain to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU. The exporter must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence acceptable to AEAT, including a valid customs export declaration (DUA/SAD), a transport document, and bank records demonstrating that the proceeds have been received in the exporting company's account. For certain internationally linked services (e.g., services physically performed on goods exported out of the EU), the 0% rate applies if the recipient is established outside the EU and the services directly relate to exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) bearing the AEAT clearance stamp or electronic validation
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR transport document as proof of physical dispatch from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT subjects export zero-rating claims to rigorous audit scrutiny. Falsified or irregular export evidence triggers: (1) regularization of unpaid VAT plus statutory late-interest; (2) an administrative penalty between 50% and 150% of the under-declared VAT under Article 191 of the General Tax Law; (3) retrospective clawback of any input VAT previously recovered in connection with the export; and (4) potential criminal liability for tax fraud under the Spanish Criminal Code if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank, acting within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism led by the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the EU Treaty's free movement of capital (Articles 63-66 TFEU). Profit remittance and dividend distributions are unrestricted for resident and non-resident shareholders, subject to standard corporate tax withholding compliance (non-resident income tax) and anti-money-laundering documentation. There are no exchange control approvals or surrender obligations; bank transfers in EUR or any convertible currency require only underlying commercial or investment documentation and compliance with SEPA/EEA reporting thresholds. Repatriation of capital introduced for the SL is deemed bona fide if the original inflow is recorded with the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) and the Commercial Register.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Bank of Spain or any authorized intermediary. Exporters may freely hold, transfer, or convert EUR and foreign currency proceeds in Spain or abroad. However, balance-of-payments and statistical declarations must be filed with the Bank of Spain via the BDP-6 form for transactions exceeding EUR 3,000,000 or where required; payments received in cash or via non-banking channels have a EUR 10,000 declaration threshold. All export invoicing and settlement must be traceable through an authorized Spanish credit institution or recognized EU payment institution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: EU Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) authorized in an EU/EEA Member State may passport into Spain under the PSD2 regime and can provide cross-border collection and disbursement services without a local license. Feasibility rating: High for transaction initiation (platform payouts, merchant settlement) but Medium Low for holding escrow capital, because Spanish commercial banks retain a dominant role for capital-escrow and credit facilities due to simplified asset protection and lower counterparty risk. Legal constraints: EMI must be passport-registered with the Bank of Spain, maintain client funds safeguarding, and comply with AML/CFT obligations. Digital-only EMIs may not be authorized to accept cash or operate correspondent banking in certain jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Spanish-registered SLs, directors may be non-resident, but onboarding protocols under Law 10/2010 on AML/CFT require positive identification. In practice, leading Spanish banks require at least one managing director or the beneficial owner to attend an in-person identity verification at the branch or via a notary in Spain. Remote onboarding using video-identification (e.g., a qualified trust service under eIDAS) is legally acceptable but many traditional banks still impose physical presence for a first-time non-resident client. A compliance-friendly alternative is to use a Spanish notary to attest the signatory's identity and powers of attorney. Without physical presence or eIDAS-compliant video identification, the application will be rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain of a wholly foreign-owned SL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of current directors/share register from the Companies House (Registro Mercantil), notarized or apostilled beneficial ownership declaration, NIE or passport copies, corporate documentation for the parent entity, and a commercial explanation for the Spanish entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth or funding for the capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from the parent company's account for the last 3-6 months, audited or certified financial statements, tax returns, and a written source-of-funds declaration. Where funds originate from a third country, ensure they originate from a reputable financial institution that is FATF-compliant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns: frequent small-value fidget toy exports to Latin America
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, purchase orders, logistics contracts, delivery documents (CMR/AWB), and customs export declarations (DUA/EXA). The business model of low-risk novelty fidget toys should align with the bank's expected merchant category code; if needed, provide quality certifications (REACH, FDA food-grade compliance) to demonstrate legitimate trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible or short-life goods without physical inspection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product specification sheets, supplier contracts, photographs, and potentially an independent inventory audit through a Spanish warehouse. Confirm that the bank's transaction monitoring is calibrated for low-risk e-commerce goods.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders inject equity through international wire transfer (SWIFT MT103 or SEPA/SCT for EU residents) using the beneficiary BLZ/IBAN of the SL's operational account. The wire must reference the corporate purpose (e.g., 'Capital contribution pursuant to shareholder resolution dated [...]') and, if the amount exceeds EUR 10,000, the Spanish bank will request a declaration of the origin of funds. The Spanish 'NIE' of the shareholder and the SL's tax ID (NIF) must be recorded. For foreign direct investment, the Statistical Register of Foreign Investments (Registro de Inversiones del Exterior) in Spain requires post-investment filing via the 'Sistema REM' for investments from non-residents, though no prior approval is necessary outside regulated sectors. To avoid misclassification, the bank should be instructed to classify the credit as 'Aportación de capital' (equity contribution), not trade revenue.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For global trade settlement, use SWIFT MT103 from the SL's bank to the foreign beneficiary's bank, or MT202 for bank-to-bank cover. For larger or secured transactions, issue a commercial letter of credit (LC) through a Spanish confirming bank with SWIFT MT700. Within the SEPA area, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCTs) and Direct Debits (SDDs) provide cost-effective euro clearing. For sales to Latin America in USD or local currencies, use USD clearing via correspondent banks (e.g., the bank's U.S. branch or via CN agent banks) or local clearing networks. The SL may also integrate platform pay rails (PayPal, Stripe, or other PSPs) for low-ticket online consumer sales, with subsequent mass reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-dated FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) up to 12 months with the SL's relationship bank for committed trade flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging market currencies without available onshore convertibility (e.g., BRL, CLP, ARS) on a non-deliverable basis
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term liquidity or balance-sheet hedging
FX options (EUR/USD calls or puts) for downside protection under a MiFID-licensed bank's ISDA/EMTA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (where the company has its corporate seat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval by the shareholders' meeting; the meeting must be held within six months of the fiscal year end. For a 31 December year-end, the latest deposit date is 30 July (approval on 30 June plus one month).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) preventing registration of any corporate act; administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000 under Article 283 of the Spanish Companies Law; in persistent cases, cancellation of the company's tax identification number (NIF) for non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month post-closing deadline. For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed from 1 July to 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 1% per month without prior assessment; late-payment interest; penalty of up to 20% of the assessed tax due. Failure to file with zero tax due generates a fixed fine of up to EUR 300 per tax period. Continued non-payment may lead to tax lien attachment and enforcement, not strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Return on Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 1 March of the year following the reporting calendar year, if any counterparty transactions exceeded EUR 3,005.06 during that year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 100 per omitted or inaccurate data item, with a minimum of EUR 1,000 for substantial omission; if the return is legally required and unfiled, the minimum sanction rises to EUR 1,500.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax Summary Declaration (Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, from 1 January to 30 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty for failure to file without payment is EUR 200; if there is tax due, a surcharge of the late-payment regime applies plus interest and penalty of up to 20% of the tax due. Habitual non-filing may be classified as an infrastructure or economic crime in serious cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for an SL if, for two consecutive fiscal years, it meets at least two of the following at year-end: (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) net annual turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit is also mandatory for entities whose shares or negotiable securities are listed on a Spanish market, credit institutions, insurers, and entities requiring consolidation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts under Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable, PGC) as approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007, including for small entities; consolidated accounts, if the SL heads a group, under EU-adopted IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose an annual UBO sacrifice return. The SL must maintain an ongoing, accurate record of its ultimate beneficial owners in the internal register. Any share transfer or UBO modification must be executed by public deed, reflected in the shareholder register and minutes ledger, and filed with the Registro de Titularidades Reales through the Registro Mercantil within 15 business days of the change. In addition, the general shareholders' meeting must review the UBO register annually when approving the yearly accounts, and directors are personally liable for failure to update the information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Shareholders)
Libro de Contratos con el Socio o Administrador (Register of Contracts with Shareholders/Directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - 1,800 per year (virtual office and fiscal representation in Madrid/Barcelona, typical EUR 75-150 per month)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if the company remains below audit thresholds; voluntary certified audit for an SME producing silicone fidgets is typically USD 7,500 - 15,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% rate on first €300,000 taxable base for new entities (first two profitable years); 10% capitalisation reserve (reserva de capitalización) reduction of taxable base equal to 10% of the positive taxable base capping at 10% when the equity increase financed by undistributed profits is maintained for 5 years; 10% leveling reserve (reserva de nivelación) for entities with net turnover < €10M; 25% R&D&IT tax credit on qualifying expenditure; 20% credit for job creation for disabled persons; 100% free-depreciation option; participation exemption at 95%/100% for qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS); unlimited offset of prior-year tax losses with a 70% annual cap for entities with turnover ≥ €20M (always 100% for SMEs with turnover < €20M); digitalisation credits per Royal Decree-Law 3/2022?
